title: Committed probe output republishes account identifiers

finding.claim: Committed probe output republishes account identifiers
finding.evidence: The generated results file also includes email addresses found in records, e.g. 'admin@example.com'. This is direct disclosure of account identifiers in a committed artifact.
finding.recommendation: Redact or suppress account-id samples in committed artifacts, or keep these outputs untracked. If the scan must be committed, report counts only and avoid embedding the matched identifiers.

code_region.note: region text is the finding's validated evidence quote; full region could not be re-located at the record head

refutation.reason: The finding claims that account identifiers are disclosed in committed artifacts. However, the code region explicitly shows that the 'account_id' entries are part of the scan's summary totals (Totals by category: account_id: 9) and per-file detail lines that list local_path, hostname, connector_name

probe.summary: `probes/gap_scan_exposure_probe.py`, result `gap-scan-exposure-pair.txt`: - The republication mechanism is real: the committed scan file prints matched strings verbatim as per-file samples (capped at 3 per category per file). The account_id samples are at lines 41, 51, 54 — **all nine hits are the single string `admin@example.com`**. - Provenance of that string: every occurrence in the underlying records sits inside a code snippet preserved in a review record — `sendmail("admin@example.com", "ABNORMALITY in {v.name}", ...)` in sample code that was itself under review (review-v12 and review-v15 records). It is example data in reviewed code, not an account identifier belonging to the operator or to any user of this system. No real identifier is exposed by this file today. - Interplay: whether committed scan/probe outputs may carry verbatim samples at all is exactly the question the public-record-profile decision (main packet #3) settles. Adopting the profile (counts-only or redacted samples in committed artifacts) gives this item its fix direction without a separate decision; the sister finding G14 shows the same mechanism carrying genuinely sensitive content.
